newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU president Ireland lauds Nobel peace laureates.
newsitem.headline: EU president Ireland lauds Nobel peace laureates.

text.p: European Union presidency Ireland welcomed the award of a Nobel Peace Prize to two East Timor independence campaigners on Friday, praising their work for "a just and peaceful solution" to the territory's conflict.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, whose country holds the EU presidency, extended "warm congratulations" to East Timor Bishop Carlos Belo and resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta.

Spring described the men's award in a news statement as a "deserving recognition for their efforts towards the achievement of a fair, comprehensive and internationally acceptable solution to the question of East Timor...".

The Norwegian Nobel Committee, sharply criticising Indonesia which invaded the territory in 1975, confirmed the body's ability to fuel controversy in a decision which was welcomed around the globe but greeted with hostility by Indonesia.
"This was about to become a forgotten conflict and we wanted to contribute to maintaining the momentum," Committee chairman Francis Sejersted told reporters at the Nobel Institute in Oslo.
"We do hope there is a message (in this award)...to the Indonesian government to change its policy."
